system_prompt:
You are a fourth-grade student taking the TIMSS mathematics test for students in your grade. Do your best on each question, as you would on a real test, using the mathematics you have learned in school so far.

The pictures, figures, and graphs of the test booklet are described in words, and its tables are written out. When a question asks you to draw, mark, shade, label, or fill in something on a figure, graph, or table, describe exactly what you would draw or write, and where. When a question asks you to show your work or explain your answer, include the work or explanation in your answer. For a multiple-choice question, choose one option.
user_prompt:
[Image: a cube for Figure A and a square-base pyramid for Figure B.]
Here are some statements about Figure A and Figure B. Put an X to show whether each statement is true or false.

| Statement | True | False |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A and B both have a square face. | X | |
| A and B both have the same number of faces. | | |
| All the angles in A are right angles. | | |
| B has more edges than A. | | |
| Some of the edges in B are curved. | | |

Figure, described in words:
Two 3-D geometric figures are shown side by side, with hidden edges represented by dashed lines. On the left, labeled 'Figure A', is a cube. On the right, labeled 'Figure B', is a square-based pyramid standing on its square base with four triangular faces meeting at a top vertex.

answer.description: Your answer to the question, as you would write it in the test booklet, with any work, explanation, or description of a drawing that the question asks for.
answer.title: Answer

output.answer:
Let's look at each statement: 

*   **A and B both have a square face.** Figure A (the cube) definitely has square faces. Figure B (the pyramid) has a square base, which is a square face. So this is **True**. I'd put an X in the 'True' column.
*   **A and B both have the same number of faces.** A cube has 6 faces. Figure B (the pyramid) has 5 faces (1 square base and 4 triangles). They don't have the same number, so this is **False**. I'd put an X in the 'False' column.
*   **All the angles in A are right angles.** A cube has right angles where the faces meet. So this is **True**. I'd put an X in the 'True' column.
*   **B has more edges than A.** A cube has 12 edges. Figure B (the pyramid) has 8 edges (4 on the base and 4 connecting the base to the top vertex). So A has more edges than B, meaning this is **False**. I'd put an X in the 'False' column.
*   **Some of the edges in B are curved.** A pyramid has straight edges, not curved ones. So this is **False**. I'd put an X in the 'False' column.
